# Eqiora Python API

Browse the modules below for classes, functions, and signatures. Start with the [Python guide](README.md) for installation and a first model.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`eqiora`](#module-eqiora) | Model authoring, numerical plans, execution, and results. |
| [`eqiora.geometry`](#module-eqiora-geometry) | Build geometry and select its regions and boundaries. |
| [`eqiora.lang`](#module-eqiora-lang) | Author Eqiora Modules, Components, expressions, and equations in Python. |
| [`eqiora.units`](#module-eqiora-units) | Units for input quantities. |
| [`eqiora.data`](#module-eqiora-data) | Explicit numeric adapters and canonical resolved-array artifacts. |
| [`eqiora.meshing`](#module-eqiora-meshing) | Plan and generate meshes from geometry. |
| [`eqiora.formulation`](#module-eqiora-formulation) | Choose a mathematical formulation and inspect the resolved choice. |
| [`eqiora.fem`](#module-eqiora-fem) | Finite-element discretization policies. |
| [`eqiora.fvm`](#module-eqiora-fvm) | Finite-volume discretization policies. |
| [`eqiora.solve`](#module-eqiora-solve) | Linear, nonlinear, and eigenvalue solver settings. |
| [`eqiora.time`](#module-eqiora-time) | Time-integration methods and related settings. |
| [`eqiora.fluid`](#module-eqiora-fluid) | Configure incompressible flow and inspect its results. |
| [`eqiora.trajectory`](#module-eqiora-trajectory) | Read spatial trajectories and derived fields. |
| [`eqiora.solid`](#module-eqiora-solid) | Configure linear elasticity and inspect structural results. |
| [`eqiora.viewer`](#module-eqiora-viewer) | Interactive, read-only views of geometry, meshes, and fields. |
| [`eqiora.colab`](#module-eqiora-colab) | Prepare a Google Colab runtime for Eqiora's notebook viewer. |
| [`eqiora.jupyter`](#module-eqiora-jupyter) | IPython extension that compiles `%%eqiora` notebook cells. |
| [`eqiora.matplotlib`](#module-eqiora-matplotlib) | Plot Eqiora results with Matplotlib. |
| [`eqiora.diff`](#module-eqiora-diff) | Implicit differentiation of Eqiora programs. |
| [`eqiora.torch`](#module-eqiora-torch) | Use Eqiora differentiable programs with PyTorch autograd. |
| [`eqiora.jax`](#module-eqiora-jax) | Use Eqiora differentiable programs with JAX. |

<a id="api-eqiora-CoordinateInterval"></a>

### `eqiora.CoordinateInterval`

Finite lower and upper bounds, in coherent SI units, for one dimensioned coordinate.

The bounds must be strictly increasing. The interval holds only the bounds and
their dimension; the support it is attached to determines which coordinate it describes.

```python
@final
class CoordinateInterval:
    def __new__(cls, lower: float, upper: float, *, dimension: Dimension) -> Self: ...
    @property
    def lower(self) -> float: ...
    @property
    def upper(self) -> float: ...
    @property
    def dimension(self) -> Dimension: ...
    def __eq__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...
    def __hash__(self) -> int: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-ExecutionSession"></a>

### `eqiora.ExecutionSession`

Step-by-step reference execution of a Model, driven by explicit input tables.

Each advance finishes stabilizing the current execution boundary before returning.

Input Ports, Clocks, and outputs can be selected by their source name or by their ULID in the Model.

```python
@final
class ExecutionSession:
    def advance(self) -> bool: ...
    @property
    def progress(self) -> dict[str, float | int]: ...
    @property
    def activation_sequence(self) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...]: ...
    def advance_ticks(self, count: int) -> int: ...
    @property
    def next_tick(self) -> Fraction | None: ...
    def checkpoint(self) -> ExecutionCheckpoint: ...
    def across(self, name: str) -> float | None: ...
    def through(self, name: str) -> float | None: ...
    def field(self, name: str) -> _TypedValue | None: ...
    def output(self, name: str, tick_index: int) -> tuple[Fraction, _TypedValue] | None: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-TrajectoryObservation"></a>

### `eqiora.TrajectoryObservation`

Terminal value or temporal reduction of an Observable over a computed trajectory.

Values use coherent SI units. A time integral has the Observable's dimension
multiplied by seconds and is computed from the solver's accepted steps, not
from the saved output samples. Extrema retain the original units and return
extremum_time_s. Closed windows include both event sides; exact computed ties
choose earliest time then accepted occurrence. No extrema derivatives or
continuous-solution error bounds are implied.

```python
@final
class TrajectoryObservation:
    @property
    def spatial_quadratures(self) -> dict[str, tuple[str, int, int]]: ...
    @property
    def extremum_time_s(self) -> float | None: ...
    @property
    def interval_s(self) -> tuple[float, float]: ...
    @property
    def endpoint_convention(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def value(self) -> _TypedValue: ...
    @property
    def value_type(self) -> ValueType: ...
    @property
    def result_identity(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def trajectory_identity(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def observable_id(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def evaluation_kind(self) -> Literal['terminal', 'time-integral', 'terminal-parameter-jvp', 'time-integral-parameter-jvp', 'time-minimum', 'time-maximum']: ...

    @property
    def parameter_jvp(self) -> bool: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-FiniteSpectrum"></a>

### `eqiora.FiniteSpectrum`

Discrete Fourier transform of uniformly spaced samples of an Observable.

The forward transform uses a `+i` exponent with a `1/N` factor and the inverse a
`-i` exponent; phases are measured from the first sample. Coefficients and
amplitudes keep the input units, power squares them, and power density and the
rectangle-transform estimate multiply them by seconds. `reconstruct_sample`
returns the windowed samples. Aliasing is not excluded, and this is not a
harmonic-response solve.

```python
@final
class FiniteSpectrum:
    @property
    def result_identity(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def trajectory_identity(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def observable_id(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def interval_s(self) -> tuple[float, float]: ...
    @property
    def phase_reference_s(self) -> float: ...
    @property
    def spacing_s(self) -> float: ...
    @property
    def sample_count(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def window(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def endpoint_convention(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def convention(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def input_type(self) -> ValueType: ...
    @property
    def coefficient_type(self) -> ValueType: ...
    @property
    def coefficients(self) -> list[Any]: ...
    def frequency_hz(self, bin: int) -> float: ...
    def angular_frequency_rad_s(self, bin: int) -> float: ...
    def phase_rad(self, bin: int, *, component: int | None=None) -> float: ...
    def amplitude(self, bin: int, *, component: int | None=None) -> float: ...
    def one_sided_amplitude(self, bin: int, *, component: int | None=None) -> float: ...
    def power(self, bin: int, *, component: int | None=None) -> float: ...
    def power_density_per_hz(self, bin: int, *, component: int | None=None) -> float: ...
    def one_sided_power_density_per_hz(self, bin: int, *, component: int | None=None) -> float: ...
    def rectangle_transform_estimate(self, bin: int) -> Any: ...
    def reconstruct_sample(self, sample: int) -> Any: ...
    def projection_type(self, projection: str) -> ValueType: ...
```

```python
    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes: ...
    def write(self, path: str | PathLike[str]) -> None: ...
    @property
    def identity(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def model_id(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def model_digest(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def model_revision(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def package_compilation_digest(self) -> str | None: ...
    @property
    def geometry_digest(self) -> str | None: ...
    @property
    def mesh_digest(self) -> str | None: ...
    @property
    def correspondence_digest(self) -> str | None: ...
    @property
    def production_digest(self) -> str | None: ...
    @property
    def realization_digest(self) -> str | None: ...
    @property
    def model(self) -> Model: ...
    @property
    def harmonic_original_model(self) -> Model | None: ...
    @property
    def harmonic_amplitudes(self) -> tuple[tuple[str, FieldRef, FieldRef], ...]: ...
    @property
    def harmonic_angular_frequency(self) -> float | None: ...
    @property
    def mesh(self) -> meshing.Mesh | None: ...
    @property
    def formulation(self) -> FormulationView | None: ...
    @property
    def capability(self) -> SpatialPlanView | solve.AlgebraicPlanView | solve.EigenPlanView | time.OdePlanView | fluid.IncompressibleFlowPlanView: ...
    @property
    def fields(self) -> tuple[FieldRef, ...]: ...
    def field_coefficient_entities(self, field: FieldRef, /) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]: ...
    def field_gradient_modes(self, field: FieldRef, /) -> dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[tuple[tuple[int, int], int], ...]]: ...
    def field_exterior_derivative(self, field: FieldRef, /) -> dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[tuple[tuple[int, int], int], ...]]: ...
    @property
    def spatial(self) -> fem.Q1 | fem.TetrahedralEdge | fem.TetrahedralFace | fem.MiniP1 | fvm.CellCenteredTpfa | fvm.CellCentered | tuple[fem.ScopedSpatialPolicy, ...] | None: ...

    def execution(self) -> ResolvedExecution: ...
    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...
    def __eq__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
    def __hash__(self) -> int: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-resolve"></a>

### `eqiora.resolve`

Combine a Model with numerical settings to produce a Plan.

The spatial, solve, and time settings choose the numerical method; they never
change the physics. The Plan keeps the Model and Mesh you pass in unchanged
(the Mesh is not regenerated). A Model without spatial fields rejects `mesh`
and `spatial`.

```python
def resolve(model: Model, *, mesh: meshing.Mesh | None=None, spatial: fem.Q1 | fem.TetrahedralEdge | fem.TetrahedralFace | fem.MiniP1 | fvm.CellCenteredTpfa | fvm.CellCentered | tuple[fem.ScopedSpatialPolicy, ...] | None=None, formulation: FormulationKind | None=None, solve: solve.Linear | solve.Newton | solve.HermitianEigen | None=None, scaling: fluid.IncompressibleScaling | dict[ConstraintRef, tuple[float, Dimension]] | None=None, temporal: time.BackwardEuler | time.Tsitouras45 | time.ImplicitMidpoint | None=None, enforcement: solve.ActiveSet | solve.StrictInterior | None=None) -> Plan: ...
```

```python
    def decode_solid(self, data: bytes) -> GeometrySolidOperation: ...
    def circular_through_cut(self, target: GeometrySolidOperation, /, *, center: tuple[float, float], radius: float, boolean_tolerance: float) -> GeometrySolidOperation: ...
    @overload
    def build(self, operation: GeometryOperation, /, *, named_topology: Mapping[str, GeometryRegionHandle | GeometryBoundaryHandle | Sequence[GeometryRegionHandle | GeometryBoundaryHandle]]) -> Geometry: ...
    @overload
    def build(self, operation: GeometrySolidOperation, /, *, named_topology: None=None) -> GeometryBuildReceipt: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-geometry-GeometryOperation"></a>

### `eqiora.geometry.GeometryOperation`

Immutable result of a primitive or Boolean geometry operation.

`boundaries` are listed in construction order: an interval returns
`(lower, upper)`, a rectangle returns
`(x_lower, x_upper, y_lower, y_upper)`, a circle returns its sole curve,
and subtract returns the four outer boundaries followed by the created cut.

```python
@final
class GeometryOperation:
    @property
    def region(self) -> GeometryRegionHandle: ...
    @property
    def boundaries(self) -> tuple[GeometryBoundaryHandle, ...]: ...
    def __eq__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-lang-Component"></a>

### `eqiora.lang.Component`

Author a public Component and bind an instance of it.

```python
@final
class Component:
    def set_notation(self, name: str, notation: Notation) -> None: ...
    def counts(self, space: FiniteSpace, components: Sequence[Expression | int]) -> Expression: ...
    def coordinates(self, space: FiniteSpace, components: Sequence[Expression | int | float | complex], *, dual: bool=False) -> Expression: ...
    def identity(self, space: FiniteSpace, *, dual: bool=False) -> Expression: ...
    def linear_map(self, source: FiniteSpace, target: FiniteSpace, rows: Sequence[Sequence[object]], *, source_dual: bool=False, target_dual: bool=False) -> Expression: ...
    def index(self, set: IndexSet, value: Expression | int) -> Expression: ...
    def sum(self, body: Callable[[Expression], object], *, over: IndexSet, name: str='i') -> Expression: ...
    def product(self, body: Callable[[Expression], object], *, over: IndexSet, name: str='i') -> Expression: ...
    def min(self, body: Callable[[Expression], object], *, over: IndexSet, name: str='i') -> Expression: ...
    def max(self, body: Callable[[Expression], object], *, over: IndexSet, name: str='i') -> Expression: ...
    def index_set(self, name: str, *, extent: int, doc: str | None=None) -> IndexSet: ...
    def event(self, name: str, guard: Expression | int | float, *, direction: Literal['any', 'rising', 'falling'], priority: int=0, doc: str | None=None) -> Event: ...
    def clock(self, name: str, *, period_s: Fraction | int, phase_s: Fraction | int=0, doc: str | None=None) -> Clock: ...
    def initial(self, *equations: tuple[object, object], left: object=None, right: object=None, doc: str | None=None) -> None: ...
    def volume(self, name: str, *, dimensions: int, doc: str | None=None) -> Support: ...
    def boundary(self, name: str, *, parent: Support, doc: str | None=None) -> Support: ...
    def complete_exterior(self, name: str, *, parent: Support, doc: str | None=None) -> BoundarySet: ...
    def boundaries(self, *members: Support) -> BoundarySelectionSet: ...
    @overload
    def parameter(self, name: str, *, value_type: Record | ImportedRecord, doc: str | None=None) -> RecordParameter: ...
    @overload
    def parameter(self, name: str, *, value_type: ValueType, doc: str | None=None) -> Expression: ...
    def coordinate(self, name: str, *, value_type: ValueType, on: Support, factor: Support, axis: int | None=..., doc: str | None=...) -> Expression: ...
    def let_alias(self, name: str, expression: Expression | int | float | complex, *, value_type: ValueType | None=None, on: Support | None=None, at: Clock | Event | None=None, doc: str | None=None) -> Expression: ...
    def property(self, name: str, *, contract: PropertyContract, doc: str | None=None) -> PropertyRequirement: ...
    @overload
    def field(self, name: str, *, on: Support | None=None, value_type: Record | ImportedRecord, role: FieldRole, at: Clock | None=None, spatial_regularity: SpatialRegularity=SpatialRegularity.Unspecified, doc: str | None=None) -> RecordField: ...
    @overload
    def field(self, name: str, *, on: Support | None=None, value_type: ValueType, role: FieldRole, at: Clock | None=None, spatial_regularity: SpatialRegularity=SpatialRegularity.Unspecified, doc: str | None=None) -> Expression: ...
    def observable(self, name: str, expression: Expression | int | float | complex, *, value_type: ValueType, on: Support | None=None, integrate_over: Support | None=None, doc: str | None=None) -> Observable: ...
    def relation(self, name: str, condition: Equation | Inequality | Complementarity, *additional_conditions: Equation | Inequality | Complementarity, on: Support | None=None, at: Clock | Event | None=None, doc: str | None=None) -> Relation: ...
    def law(self, name: str, *, on: Support, flux: Expression, source: Expression, storage: Expression | None=None, doc: str | None=None) -> Relation: ...
    def test(self, name: str, *, for_: Expression, dimension: Dimension | None=None, regularity: str | None=None, zero_on: Support | BoundarySelectionSet | None=None) -> Expression: ...
    def weak_form(self, name: str, relations: Sequence[Relation], *, equations: Sequence[tuple[object, object]], doc: str | None=None) -> None: ...
    def harmonic_form(self, name: str, relations: Sequence[Relation], *, angular_frequency: object, convention: str, normalization: str, excitations: Sequence[tuple[Expression, object]], amplitudes: Sequence[tuple[str, Expression, ValueType]], doc: str | None=None) -> None: ...
    def port(self, name: str, *, connector: Connector, on: Support | None=None, doc: str | None=None) -> Port | FieldPort: ...
    def connect(self, *ports: Port, over: BoundaryMember | None=None, doc: str | None=None) -> None: ...
    def connect_periodic(self, first: FieldPort, second: FieldPort, *, doc: str | None=None) -> None: ...
    def instance(self, name: str, *, component: Component | ComponentRef, bindings: Mapping[str, object], doc: str | None=None) -> Mapping[str, Expression | Port]: ...
    def clock_requirement(self, name: str, *, doc: str | None=None) -> Clock: ...
    def field_requirement(self, name: str, *, value_type: ValueType, role: FieldRole, on: Support | None=None, at: Clock | None=None, spatial_regularity: SpatialRegularity=SpatialRegularity.Unspecified, doc: str | None=None) -> Expression: ...
    def set_default(self, parameter: Expression, value: Expression | int | float | complex) -> None: ...
    def input(self, name: str, *, value_type: ValueType, on: Support | None=None, at: Clock | None=None, spatial_regularity: SpatialRegularity=SpatialRegularity.Unspecified, doc: str | None=None) -> Expression: ...
    def output(self, name: str, *, value_type: ValueType, on: Support | None=None, at: Clock | None=None, spatial_regularity: SpatialRegularity=SpatialRegularity.Unspecified, doc: str | None=None) -> Expression: ...
```

```python
    def __truediv__(self, other: Expression | float | int | complex, /) -> Expression: ...
    def __rtruediv__(self, other: float | int, /) -> Expression: ...
    def __pow__(self, exponent: int, /) -> Expression: ...
    def __bool__(self) -> bool: ...
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool: ...
    def __ne__(self, other: object) -> bool: ...
    def __lt__(self, other: object) -> bool: ...
    def __le__(self, other: object) -> bool: ...
    def __gt__(self, other: object) -> bool: ...
    def __ge__(self, other: object) -> bool: ...
    def __neg__(self) -> Expression: ...
    def __getitem__(self, index: int | Expression | slice) -> Expression: ...
```

```python
    def component(self, name: str, *, doc: str | None=None) -> Component: ...
    def model(self, name: str, *, doc: str | None=None) -> Component: ...
    def property_contract(self, name: str, *, value_type: ValueType, inputs: Mapping[str, ValueType] | None=None, derivatives: Literal['value_only', 'first_partials', 'first_open_intervals']='value_only', branch: str | None=None, doc: str | None=None) -> PropertyContract: ...

    def property_release(self, name: str, *, implements: PropertyContract, value: Expression | int | float | complex | Sequence[object], source_unit: Unit, source_scale: int | float, citation: str, license: str, validity: Expression | bool | None=None, branch: str | None=None, outside: Literal['reject']='reject', doc: str | None=None) -> PropertyRelease: ...
    def material_composition(self, name: str, *, properties: Mapping[str, PropertyRelease], doc: str | None=None) -> MaterialComposition: ...

    def write_eqi(self, path: str | PathLike[str]) -> None: ...
```

Mesh a rectangle with a structured grid of affine triangles.

Each grid cell is split along its lower-left to upper-right diagonal. You
choose only the (positive) number of subdivisions in each direction.

```python
    @property
    def cells(self) -> tuple[int, int]: ...
    @property
    def diagonal(self) -> str: ...
    def __eq__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...
```

```python
    def __eq__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-meshing-Mesh"></a>

### `eqiora.meshing.Mesh`

Immutable mesh, linked to the geometry and plan that produced it.

```python
@final
class Mesh:
    @staticmethod
    def coordinate_factors(model: Model, domain: DomainRef, cells_per_factor: list[int]) -> Mesh: ...
    @staticmethod
    def from_bytes(data: bytes) -> Mesh: ...
    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes: ...
    def refine(self, marked_cells: Iterable[int], /, *, maximum_cells: int) -> Mesh: ...
    @property
    def source_digest(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def realized_geometry_digest(self) -> str | None: ...
    @property
    def digest(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def correspondence_digest(self) -> str | None: ...
    @property
    def production_lineage_bytes(self) -> bytes: ...
    @property
    def production_lineage_digest(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def canonical_bytes(self) -> bytes: ...
    @property
    def dimension(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def vertex_count(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def cell_count(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def coordinates(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]: ...
    @property
    def cells(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.uint32]: ...
    def entity_vertices(self, entity: tuple[int, int]) -> tuple[int, ...]: ...
    @property
    def minimum_mean_ratio(self) -> float: ...
    @property
    def selection_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]: ...
    def selection_entity_count(self, name: str | GeometrySelection) -> int: ...
    def selection_entities(self, name: str | GeometrySelection) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]: ...
    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-solve-EigenExclusion"></a>

### `eqiora.solve.EigenExclusion`

Directions removed from the eigenproblem, with separate nullspace tests for the operator and the metric.

Defects are normalized Frobenius norms of the operator or metric acting on
the excluded directions. The null flags compare them with the Plan's
residual tolerance; they do not identify a physical gauge. The
dimensionless projector can be oblique in coefficient space.

```python
@final
class EigenExclusion:
    @property
    def dimension(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def projector(self) -> Any: ...
    @property
    def projector_type(self) -> ValueType: ...
    @property
    def operator_defect(self) -> float: ...
    @property
    def metric_defect(self) -> float: ...
    @property
    def tolerance(self) -> float: ...
    @property
    def is_operator_null(self) -> bool: ...
    @property
    def is_metric_null(self) -> bool: ...
```

<a id="api-eqiora-solve-Newton"></a>

### `eqiora.solve.Newton`

as the Newton absolute tolerance, so that an unconverged iteration cannot
stop on a zero correction.


<a id="api-eqiora-diff-compile"></a>

### `eqiora.diff.compile`

Compile a differentiable program over an ordered set of parameters.

For a finite affine Plan, the inputs are real or complex Parameters, scalar or
shaped, and outputs are ordered real/complex Fields or Observables;
the Plan must not require state. Complex derivatives use the real differential
with the pairing Re(sum(conj(a)*b)), so dependence on the conjugate is kept.
Input coordinates are ordered by selection, then row-major by component, then
real before imaginary part. The input identities count Parameters; the input
shape counts real coordinates. A finite nonlinear Plan also needs its exact seed.

```python
def compile(plan: Plan, *, inputs: Sequence[ParameterRef], outputs: Sequence[FieldRef | ObservableRef], state: State | None=None) -> DifferentiableProgram: ...
```
